tools.name: get_availability
tools.description:
Bookable times at one venue, on one date, for one party size.

        `date` is the venue's own local calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Each slot carries a
        `slot_id` to pass to book and a `starts_at` that is a full venue-local datetime, so
        a service running past midnight is unambiguous w

tools.name: book
tools.description:
Book a table. This takes a real table at a real restaurant.

        Pass a `slot_id` from get_availability. Confirm the venue, date, time and party size
        with the person before calling this, and do not call it speculatively: there is no
        cancel tool, so a booking made by mistake has t

tools.name: get_reservation
tools.description:
Read one booking this credential made back from the venue.

        Use it to confirm a booking landed. A `status` of `pending` means the venue has not
        answered yet, not that it failed; treat anything you do not recognise as
        non-terminal rather than reporting a failure.

tools.name: join_waitlist
tools.description:
Ask to be told if a table opens at a time the guest actually wants.

        This is not a reservation and never becomes one by itself. The venue contacts the
        guest if something frees up, so say that plainly rather than implying a table is
        held.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Book a table. This takes a real table at a real restaurant. Pass a `slot_id` from get_availability. Confirm the venue, date, time and party size with the person…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: join_waitlist · Private data: get_reservation, join_waitlist · Public sink: book, join_waitlist.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: join_waitlist · Private data: get_reservation, join_waitlist · Public sink: book, join_waitlist

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_venues" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
